Hi Jonas / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to surface a couple items so we can get the MSA + Order Form over the finish line: specifically the audit rights language in the security exhibit and the pen-test notice window. We attached our annotated redline (Medinova_Security_Exhibit_Redline_v1.docx) with comments. High level asks:
- Do you support a 30-day notice for an external penetration test, with a mutually agreed 3-day staging access window?
- Can Redwood commit to a quarterly evidence cadence for SOC 2 reports and an S3 bucket of artifacts (read-only URL) for the sample sets?
- We need a short ticketing workflow: who on Redwood's side takes evidence requests and SLA for replies (we typically ask for 5 business days).

We'd like a quick alignment call next week to close timing — procurement is aiming to sign by June 18.

Attached: Medinova_Security_Exhibit_Redline_v1.docx, OrderForm_Medinova_2027.pdf

Thanks,
Anna Gladstone\Lead, Vendor Risk & Procurement\MediNova Therapeutics
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Anna Gladstone <anna.gladstone@medinova.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit redline + sequencing questions

Anna — thanks for the redline and clear asks. Quick answers up front, then proposed path: 

Short answers:
- Pen-test notice: we are comfortable with 30-day notice for external tests; we usually require a 48-72 hour staging access window to support ephemeral creds and monitoring hooks, but we can negotiate a 3-day explicit window for this engagement if needed (we'll capture that in the exhibit).
- SOC 2 evidence cadence: we can provide quarterly SOC 2 reports and a read-only S3 link for sampled artifacts under a controlled access policy. We cannot continuously expose raw PII-containing logs; artifacts will be scoped to assertion-relevant evidence and redacted where necessary.
- Ticketing / SLA: Redwood Support (security-evidence@redwood.com) will triage evidence requests. Proposed SLA: initial triage within 2 business days, evidence delivery target 5 business days for standard artifacts, 10 business days for staging access requests that require infra coordination.

Proposed path:
1) Kimberly to produce a two-page redline summary for legal (order form + exhibit) — she'll flag any non-negotiable clauses.
2) I will draft a short evidence playbook (one page) that we can attach to the Order Form as an exhibit; includes ticketing flow, contact points, and typical timelines.
3) Ops (Ben) will propose a pen-test calendar with a 7-day preferred window and a 3-day staging access carveout we can reserve.

Can we target a 30-minute call Monday (6/7) at 10am PT? If so, I'll share an agenda and the evidence playbook draft beforehand.

— Jonas Weber\Director, Security & Trust\Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, Anna Gladstone <anna.gladstone@medinova.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit redline + sequencing questions

Anna / team — I've reviewed the annotated redline and pulled a few legal observations (summary below). I'll circulate a compact redline (tracked) by end of day Friday. Key items to confirm: 

Legal highlights (summary):
- Audit rights: Medinova's request for unlimited inspection is too broad. We will propose scoped inspection tied to SOC 2 assertions and predefined evidence buckets (linked in the evidence matrix).
- Penetration testing: agree to 30-day notice, we will add a clause for coordination and a mutual blackout period for major releases. We will explicitly exclude third-party vendor tests that require system-level access beyond documented scope.
- Data access & redaction: we must preserve Redwood's obligation to redact or withhold PII from artifact exports; we will provide sample manifests for each evidence delivery.
- SLA language: we can accept a 5 business day evidence target for standard artifacts; for anything requiring infra work (staging creds, expanded packet captures), we need the 10 business day carveout.

I'll attach the redline summary and a lightweight evidence matrix template (evidence_matrix_template.xlsx). We should keep the evidence playbook short and operational rather than legalese to avoid back-and-forth.

Kimberly Park\Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security\Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Anna Gladstone <anna.gladstone@medinova.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit redline + sequencing questions

Anna — operational notes from the pen-test perspective: 

- Preferred pen-test timing: we can hold a reserved window on our calendar the week of July 12–16. That gives us time to complete the DocuSign flow and scheduling. If Medinova needs an earlier test, propose July 5–9 as a contingency.
- Staging access: our staging environment will support ephemeral SSH/API keys scoped for the test; we will require a test plan and an IP allowlist 7 days ahead of the test.
- Evidence packaging: typical deliverable is a zip with: SOC 2 report (PDF), consolidated manifest (CSV), redacted sample artifacts, and the evidence manifest. We'll drop those into a read-only S3 bucket and provide a presigned URL that expires in 30 days.
- Contact points: security-evidence@redwood.com (primary), infra-oncall@redwood.com (escalation).

I'll join the call Monday and bring a sample ticket and sample manifest to walk through.

— Ben Carter\Security Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
